faq: Which ERP and shipping tools can you connect?

Common ones such as SAP Business One, NetSuite, Odoo, QuickBooks, Xero, ShipStation, UPS, FedEx and DHL. If the system has an API or a Magento extension, we can usually link it. Name it in the order form.
Do I need to buy an extension for each connection?
Sometimes. Many tools sell their own Magento extension, which is paid to them. We pick the cheapest sound route and tell you the cost before building. A small custom connector is often cheaper.
Can you sync products to Amazon or eBay?

Yes, using the marketplace's official APIs or a trusted connector, and following each marketplace's listing rules. We do not set up anything that breaks their policies, such as scraped data or duplicated listings.
What happens if a connection stops working?
We add error alerts and retry logic, so a failed sync is noticed and retried. Ongoing monitoring is a separate service, and we explain how to restart a link if it fails.
desc:
Magento integrations for ERP and shipping connect your store to the systems that run orders, stock, labels and accounts. Ecom Swift LLC sets up and tests these links in your own Magento store, so data moves between tools without retyping.

## What are Magento integrations?

A Magento integration is a connection that passes data between your store and another business system. Common examples are an order feed to an ERP or accounting tool, stock levels coming from a warehouse system, carrier rates and tracking numbers from a shipping provider, and product listings sent to a marketplace.

Each connection uses either the other tool's official Magento extension or its API. When neither fits, a small connector module can bridge the gap.

## Why manual order handling stops working

When a store is small, copying orders into an accounting tool feels harmless. As volume grows, the copying becomes a daily chore, and chores produce mistakes. A stock number updated by hand lags behind real inventory, so the store sells an item that is not on the shelf. A tracking number pasted late brings a wave of customer emails.

Connecting the systems moves that routine work to software. Your team then spends its time on exceptions instead of repetition.

## How integrations affect cost, quality and customers

The main effect is time saved and fewer errors. An order that flows to your ERP the moment it is paid needs no retyping, and a stock level that updates itself reduces overselling. Shipping rates shown at checkout from the carrier match what you will actually be charged.

Customers feel the difference in smaller ways: accurate availability, quick dispatch and tracking links that arrive on time. Results vary with the quality of your source data and the speed of the systems involved, so we test with real orders rather than promise exact outcomes.

## What a well-built Magento integration includes

- A written map showing which data moves, in which direction and how often.
- The official extension or API of the other tool, chosen over custom code where it fits.
- Order export to ERP or accounting, with taxes, shipping and discounts mapped correctly.
- Stock synchronization from the warehouse, on a schedule that suits your sales volume.
- Carrier rates at checkout and tracking numbers pushed back to the order.
- Marketplace listings and order import, where your plan includes them.
- Clear handling of failed calls, with retries and alerts to a named person.
- An error log that is readable by a non-developer.
- Test orders covering refunds, partial shipments and cancellations.
- A short integration note listing credentials owners, endpoints and what to do when a link stops.

## How we connect your systems

We start by listing every system involved and what each one should do. Then we decide, for each connection, whether an official extension or an API call is the safer choice for your setup.

Work happens on staging first. We place test orders and watch them travel through each system, comparing totals, tax and stock at each end. Only when the figures match do we switch the connection on for the live store, with alerts active from the start.

The Basic package sets up one integration end to end. The Standard package covers up to three, such as order export, carrier rates and stock sync. The Premium package adds marketplace sync, a small custom connector, a retry and alert system and a payment tool, along with an integration map and a period of fixes.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Name one person who owns each connected system.
- Clean up product codes and SKUs before connecting anything.
- Decide which system is the source of truth for stock.
- Test unusual orders such as returns and split shipments.
- Keep your own copy of API credentials in a safe place.

**Avoid:**
- Connecting two systems that both try to edit the same stock number.
- Running syncs every minute when hourly updates would do.
- Ignoring alert emails after the first week.
- Buying a separate extension for a task the tool's own connector already handles.
- Going live on a Friday evening without anyone watching.

## Who it is for

This service suits a merchant whose staff export orders to a spreadsheet every day and then type them into accounting software. It also suits a store with a physical warehouse that needs stock to stay accurate across channels. A third case is a seller who wants to add a marketplace channel without managing two catalogs by hand.

## What we need from you

Send the list of tools you want to connect, the plan or edition each one uses and any API details their support provides. We need collaborator, staff or developer access to Magento and a separate user in each tool where possible. We never need your passwords, and you pay any extension makers or software providers directly.
